paper_role: pre-registered numeric predictions for the five closed-form placement laws, to be scored against fresh measurements on the new node (prediction error is itself a reported result; the 2026-08 Gram-tap estimate missed by 40x)

frozen_system.hardware: trn2.3xlarge, one Trainium2 device, 4 logical NeuronCores (LNC=2), 96 GiB HBM
frozen_system.parallelism: TP4, CP1, no CFG-parallel, SP off (the qualified A12 topology)
frozen_system.compiled_root: recorded in the result file (artifact hash), not known before compile

scoring: a law counts as predictive if the measured value falls within 2x of the point prediction (or inside the predicted range where a range is given); misses are reported, not re-fitted

L1_dispatch_floor.statement: A graph invocation on an AOT accelerator has a fixed cost independent of its arithmetic; control logic moved on-device can recover at most the host critical-path cost it removes.
L1_dispatch_floor.measurement: H1a-style weightless K=2 predictor graph, 100 timed device calls (scripts/run_flux_h1a_resident_state.py); host predictor timing from CacheRunner on the same tensors

L2_alias_tax.statement: Fusing work into an existing graph call is free only if it needs no cross-invocation resident state; an aliased output adds a fixed per-call cost independent of its size.
L2_alias_tax.measurement: gram-tap backbone variants post / noalias / bf16 vs baseline, 30 host-side wall-clock calls each, same entry and inputs (difflet/backends/trainium/flux/gram_tap.py)

L3_numerical_boundary.statement: A graph boundary is a numerical-semantics boundary: an intermediate dtype cast inside one AOT graph is not a contract; the compiler may fuse across it.
L3_numerical_boundary.measurement: H1c single-NEFF vs split cache-step runners over the fixed A12 50-step schedule with synthetic anchors (scripts/run_flux_h1c_resident_cache_step.py)

L4_weight_streaming_floor.statement: Any full-depth backbone pass pays weight streaming HBM->SBUF plus per-layer collective floors even at zero tokens; partial-step mechanisms (residual split, token subsets) cannot beat host-side skipping at a 3.95x operating point because they must displace an anchor to pay for themselves (38*c < 267*dA => c < 7 ms per displaced anchor).

intercept_ms_shape_ladder.basis: weights 5.95 GB/core at ~0.73 TB/s = 8.2 ms + 114 all-reduce floors x 7 us = 0.8 ms + dispatch 0.34 ms; overlap may hide part of it

L4_weight_streaming_floor.measurement: compile FLUX TP4 at 256^2, 512^2, 768^2, 1024^2 (256/1024/2304/4096 image tokens + 512 text); fit step_ms = F + a*N + b*N^2 by least squares over per-step medians; report F with its CI

L5_amortization_bound.statement: Batching (cohort, CFG, DP lanes) can recover at most the token-independent fixed cost F per step: G(B) = F(1-1/B)/t1.
L5_amortization_bound.measurement: compile FLUX TP4 1024^2 at B=2; paired per-step timing B=1 vs B=2 on the same prompts (24 pairs, AB/BA alternated, prompt-stratified bootstrap as in the H1e protocol)
L5_amortization_bound.stop_condition: t2/t1 > 1.96 on FLUX and Wan -> the batching section is dropped and only this bound row remains

L6_video_crossover_corollary.statement: Host-side cache control stays optimal until the anchor tensor is large enough that host tensor algebra plus PCIe transfer exceeds the on-device dispatch+alias cost: S* where 3*S/BW_host = 0.34 ms + 3.1 ms.

prediction.consequence: no default single-chip video configuration crosses; resident state stays rejected for video

L6_video_crossover_corollary.measurement: host predictor + scheduler timing vs anchor size on synthetic tensors 0.5 MB .. 512 MB (CPU only), and the L1/L2 device constants

quality_policy: Only designs that change outputs (asymmetric CFG schedules, video schedules) are scored, and only with the existing frozen ImageReward/VQAScore contract; no new thresholds are fitted. Pure architecture comparisons (batching, TP layout, policy switching) must be bit-exact.
